terms.definition: The proportions of sand, silt and clay particles in a soil.
terms.examiner: It controls drainage, aeration and nutrient retention; found with a soil triangle.

terms.definition: A soil with a balance of sand, silt and clay.
terms.examiner: Drains well but holds water and nutrients, so is the most fertile texture.
Holds water and nutrients and binds particles into crumbs, reducing erosion.

terms.definition: The loss of soluble nutrients from soil as water drains through it.
terms.examiner: Worst on sandy soils and after heavy rain.

terms.definition: The removal of soil by wind or water faster than it forms.
terms.examiner: Know the causes (bare soil, steep slopes, overgrazing) and the controls (contour ploughing, terraces, windbreaks, cover crops).

terms.definition: An equation that estimates the rate of soil erosion from rainfall, soil erodibility, slope, crop cover and management factors.
terms.examiner: Used to compare the effect of changing a farming practice.

terms.definition: The degradation of land in dry areas until it can no longer support vegetation.
terms.examiner: Caused by overgrazing, deforestation and poor irrigation as well as climate.
